A weak disturbance dubbed Invest 95W (discussed in the Tropical 
Systems section below) by the Joint Typhoon Warning Center (JTWC) 
will bring scattered showers and isolated thunderstorms tonight
through Saturday night across the region. Conditions will remain
below hazardous criteria, so no Watches, Warnings, and Advisories 
(WWAs) were issued at this time. 95W will pass between Guam and Rota
over the next day, so conditions are expected to quickly improve on 
Sunday. The heaviest convection and showers are found along its 
southern peripheries, so the zones were split between Guam and the 
CNMI to account for a higher concentration of showers over the 
southern tip of the island chain. Gentle to moderate winds are 
expected through the weekend with a counterclockwise change in 
direction through Saturday, eventually becoming gentle 
northwesterlies early next week. Then, a dry spell will ensue across 
the region, with the possibility of isolated showers and light and 
variable winds during the former half of next week. Active weather 
may return late next week as models hint at a potential tropical 
disturbance approaching the islands from the east. Since the 
timeframe is beyond the next five days, uncertainty is high, but we 
will continue monitoring this situation. As a reminder, October is 
within peak typhoon season in the western Pacific, so residents of 
the Marianas should monitor the forecast over the next several days 
and maintain a general state of preparedness.

Marine...
Altimetry indicates combined seas of 5 to 7 ft. A long-period
northeasterly swell emanating from Typhoon Koguma (27W) will keep
seas and surf along north and east facing reefs elevated. However,
marine conditions are still expected to remain below hazardous
criteria. There is a moderate risk of rip currents along north, east,
and west facing reefs. South facing reefs were removed from that risk
as this morning's observations supported surf lower than previously 
anticipated. As Invest 95W crosses the Marianas, numerous showers and
isolated thunderstorms with fresh gusts are expected in Guam's
southern coastal waters tonight and Saturday. Scattered showers and
isolated thunderstorms are forecast elsewhere in the region.

Tropical Systems...
At 1 PM, TY Koguma was located 670 miles east of Alamagan, centered 
near 19N156E, moving west-northwest at 13 mph. Maximum sustained 
winds have increased to 100 mph. TY Koguma is expected to continue 
to move west-northwest, slowly turning northwest over the next couple
of days as it continues to strengthen. TY Koguma is forecast to 
strengthen over the next 24 hours, increasing to around 135 mph 
Saturday, which would make Koguma a Category 4 typhoon.

For more information on TY Koguma, please refer to bulletins issued
by the Joint Typhoon Warning Center under WMO header WTPN33 PGTW and
by the National Weather Service under WMO header WTPQ33 PGUM.

A weak tropical disturbance, Invest 95W, is found along the monsoon
trough southwest of Guam near 13.5N 144.5E. Invest 95W is currently 
rated sub-low, meaning development is not expected for the next few 
days. The current synoptic pattern over the area does not favor 
development of 95W for at least the next several days. Invest 95W 
looks to drift north over the coming days as it slowly weakens.

Eastern Micronesia...
Eastern Micronesia is transitioning from a dry pattern to an overall
wetter, unsettled pattern. Convection has increased a bit earlier
than previously expected at Majuro, with scattered showers and
isolated thunderstorms over the atoll today. POPs (Probability of
Precipitation) now look to remain in the 40 to 50 percent range
through the middle of next week. For Pohnpei and Kosrae, POPs in the
10 to 20 percent range look to continue through Sunday night at both
locations, then increase to the 30 to 40 percent range the beginning
of next week. POPs look to remain around 30 percent through the
middle of next week at Kosrae, and 40 to 50 percent range for
Pohnpei. The increased convection across eastern Micronesia can be
attributed to the monsoon trough. As TY Koguma pulls off to the
west-northwest, the monsoon trough will move over the region. The
trough is already pulling closer to the Marshalls, resulting in
increased convection today. As Koguma moves farther west-northwest,
the trough will move into Pohnpei and clip Kosrae. However, most of 
the associated showers will be north of Kosrae.

For the marine forecast, no major changes expected. Overall, benign
seas will continue through the beginning of next week. Latest model
guidance is showing a weak disturbance developing north of the
Marshalls and Kosrae that could result in increased seas next week.
Mostly gentle to moderate winds are expected at Majuro and Kosrae,
with winds increasing to gentle to moderate at Pohnpei early next
week.
